November 6, 2026

Stephen Miller named White House chief of staff as Susie Wiles exits

tags: politics, government
sources: @aaronparnas, @groundnews, @oafnation_actual, @total.hypocrisy

Trump announced on Truth Social that deputy chief of staff Stephen Miller will become White House chief of staff starting Monday, November 9, 2026, with Susie Wiles moving to the Trump political operation. Wiles, the first woman to hold the role and Trump's longest-serving chief of staff, reportedly submitted her resignation Thursday night after days of public calls from Republicans for her removal following the midterm losses. Representative Robert Garcia, who leads the Oversight Committee, responded that "Stephen Miller should lawyer up," saying Democrats will continue investigating Miller's conduct and contest his policies in Congress and the courts. Miller's record on federalizing the National Guard, directing federal law enforcement resources to local police, and pursuing cases against left-wing organizations has been cited as grounds for concern about the scope of the role.

Three senior Justice Department officials resign in two days

tags: politics, legal
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

John Eisenberg, the assistant attorney general for national security, resigned Friday, according to Politico. He is the third senior Justice Department official to depart since the midterm elections, after Civil Rights Division chief Harmeet Dhillon resigned Thursday and US Attorney for the Southern District of Florida Jason Reding Quinones resigned Friday, a departure confirmed by Attorney General Todd Blanche. Quinones's office oversaw the conspiracy investigation into Trump's political opponents, and Eisenberg had led the National Security Division since June 2025. A member of Congress said departing officials remain subject to subpoena and could be called to testify under oath.

Democrats post largest legislative gains since 1974 as maps shift

tags: politics, elections
sources: @aaronparnas

Democrats secured the most legislative seats in any election since 1974, including an Arizona trifecta of the state House, state Senate and governor's office for the first time in 60 years, with Governor Hobbs re-elected. In Texas, James Talarico defeated Ken Paxton by about 12 points, winning more early votes than Paxton received in total; the Wall Street Journal reported Trump privately regrets endorsing Paxton over John Cornyn. According to Politico, Republicans are alarmed about 2028 prospects as the results put Ohio and Georgia in play, while lawyers are advising White House staffers on exposure to congressional investigations and some staff are weighing whether to leave.

Hegseth faces likely House impeachment vote and is ruled out for Senate seat

tags: politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas, @oafnation_actual

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth faces a likely House impeachment vote next week, with more Republicans expected to support it. A source close to Tennessee's incoming governor told USA Today that Hegseth is not a candidate to replace Senator Marsha Blackburn, who was elected governor on November 3 and will name her own successor; reporting from Punchbowl indicated Hegseth had been seeking the seat and Blackburn's team rejected the idea. A five-minute video Hegseth released outside the Defense Department defending his record drew further criticism. An impeachment in the House would require a Senate trial, an outcome the administration is said to want to avoid.

US offers $20 million for information on Iran's nuclear program

tags: politics, defence
sources: @aaronparnas, @hunteralexanderhowell

The State Department's Rewards for Justice program is offering up to $20 million, plus possible relocation, for information about Iran's nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment and associated personnel. The offer was circulated by US Central Command. It follows earlier administration statements that Iran's nuclear program had been destroyed in US strikes.

Trump calls elections crooked and demands Alaska votes be reassigned

tags: politics, elections
sources: @oafnation_actual

Trump told reporters Thursday that "our elections are so crooked, you have no idea," according to AFP. He posted that votes cast for a candidate he called the "Fake" Sullivan and for Gerald Heikes should be awarded to Senator Dan Sullivan. Democrat Mary Peltola leads the uncalled Alaska Senate race 48.2% to 47.9%.

Houston bars police from contacting ICE over minor offenses

tags: immigration, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Houston Mayor John Whitmire signed an order Friday barring city police from contacting Immigration and Customs Enforcement over nonviolent, non-jailable offenses, according to the Associated Press. Under the order, ICE may be contacted only in the case of a jailable arrest or an administrative warrant. Whitmire described the change as a consequence of Democratic wins in Texas.

Finland accuses US of playing politics with Patriot missiles for Ukraine

tags: war, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Finnish Defence Minister Antti Häkkänen told Euronews that European states have already paid for Patriot interceptors intended for Ukraine but Washington has not approved their delivery. President Zelenskyy said Ukraine has waited nearly a month for Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to sign off on the transfer. The delay comes as Russia prepares large winter attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure.

Incoming Texas governor requests pause on state land sales to Musk companies

tags: politics, markets
sources: @aaronparnas

Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa has requested a pause on all state land sales to Elon Musk's companies, including the sale of Boca Chica State Park to SpaceX, according to Bloomberg. She told CNN that a working relationship with Musk's companies is possible but "it has to be on our terms. It cannot be just running over the people of Texas." Shares in Musk's companies fell after election night, and roughly $400 million he invested in races across the country did not produce wins.

Washington and Colorado voters approve transgender athlete restrictions

tags: politics, legal
sources: @groundnews

Voters in Washington and Colorado passed ballot initiatives restricting transgender students' participation in school athletics, with Washington's measure drawing more than 56% support and Colorado's 52%. Washington will exclude biologically male students from girls' teams and require medical providers to certify eligibility for female competition, while Colorado will require schools and athletic organizations to classify teams by sex or as coed, with participation tied to birth sex. Supporters took the proposals directly to voters after Democratic governors and lawmakers in both states declined to pass bans. More than half of US states now have some form of restriction on transgender athletes.

Chinese court takes up COVID defamation suit against Missouri officials

tags: legal, health
sources: @groundnews

A court in Wuhan has accepted a defamation case brought against the state of Missouri and three people who have led its attorney general's office: Eric Schmitt, Andrew Bailey and Catherine Hanaway. The city government, the Wuhan Institute of Virology and the Chinese Academy of Sciences allege the defendants spread falsehoods about the coronavirus pandemic and seek an apology, reputational remedies and damages, with the South China Morning Post reporting a compensation demand of 356.44 billion yuan. The case follows Missouri's April 2020 lawsuit seeking compensation from Hubei province and other Chinese defendants for economic harm attributed to the pandemic.

Midterm ad spending reached $11.87 billion across all races

tags: politics, elections
sources: @groundnews

Total advertising spending for the 2026 midterms, including primaries and every federal, state and local race and ballot measure, reached $11.87 billion, according to AdImpact data as of November 2. Democrats accounted for $5.45 billion, Republicans $5.02 billion and independent and issue groups $1.40 billion. The Ohio Senate race drew the most, with $300.3 million behind winner Sherrod Brown against $218.2 million for Jon Husted, followed by Texas, where James Talarico's side spent $282.5 million to Ken Paxton's $147.5 million. In Michigan, Maine and Alaska the losing or trailing Republican side outspent the Democratic side.

Utah congressional races remain uncalled as ballot curing deadlines approach

tags: elections, politics
sources: @carolinegleich

Ballots are still being counted in Utah, where Republican congressional candidates hold less than half the statewide vote and Democrats trail by under one percent. Several state legislative races in Summit, Morgan, Rich, Davis and Wasatch counties are separated by a few hundred votes or fewer. Voters whose ballots were flagged for a missing or mismatched signature, an omitted ID number, a recent move, provisional status or first-time registration can check status at vote.utah.gov and return a cure form with ID. Most counties require cure forms by noon on Monday, November 16, while Wasatch County's deadline is 5 p.m. Tuesday, November 10.

Van Hollen rules out challenging Schumer for Senate Democratic leader

tags: politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

Senator Chris Van Hollen told Fox 5 DC that he is "not looking to be the next Democratic leader" and is considering a 2028 presidential run. The statement removes one potential challenger to Chuck Schumer's position as Senate Democratic leader. Senator-elect Abdul El-Sayed told CNN that Van Hollen would be an "amazing" majority leader.

Drug patent tactics blamed for US prescription costs as EPIC Act push grows

tags: health, politics
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

Pharmaceutical manufacturers are accused of using patent practices that delay generic competition and keep US prescription prices high. The practices named are patent thickets, product hopping and pay-for-delay arrangements, in which brand manufacturers pay potential generic competitors to stay out of the market. Supporters are urging constituents to contact members of Congress in support of the EPIC Act, described as having bipartisan backing.

White House postpones tech panel meeting with Huang and Zuckerberg

tags: tech, politics
sources: @oafnation_actual

The Trump administration has postponed a White House technology panel meeting that was to include Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang and Meta chief executive Mark Zuckerberg, according to Reuters. No new date was given.

Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern merger draws support from logistics executives

tags: markets, economy
sources: @hunteralexanderhowell

A proposed merger between Union Pacific and Norfolk Southern would create a coast-to-coast rail network. The chief executive of Schneider said the combination could bring greater connectivity, faster transit and more reliable infrastructure, citing a comparable cross-border model developed with Mexico that improved the company's operations and consumer outcomes. Other analysts have said the merger would reduce transit times and open new markets and jobs.

Fox lists 2028 Republican contenders as post-midterm jockeying begins

tags: politics, elections
sources: @oafnation_actual

A Fox News segment presented a list of potential 2028 Republican presidential contenders attributed to Newt Gingrich. The names included Vance, Rubio, Cruz, Cotton, DeSantis, Hegseth and Youngkin. The segment framed the field as the start of a contest over the direction of the movement after the midterms.
